summary: Vidya Niwas Mishra specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at the University of Allahabad under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya and at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University. He served as Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1989) and Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1986–1989).

Vilhelm Thomsen was a Danish scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned his PhD from the University of Copenhagen (1859–1869). He held several posts there, including Professor (1887–1913), and served as President of the Royal Danish Academy in 1909.
Vimalaraṁsi studied under Sayadaw U Silananda and Anagarika Munindra.

Vincenc Lesný was an Indologist who studied at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts (~1903–1907) under Moriz Winternitz and Josef Zubatý. He held a post at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts from ~1918 to 1953.

Vincent Arthur Smith, an Indologist and historian/archaeologist, studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1865–1869). He served in the Indian Civil Service as Commissioner of Gorakhpur (1871–1900) and later as Curator at the University of Oxford (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (MA by 1996, PhD by 2012), under Lucia Dolce, and at Taisho, Hanazono, and Kyoto universities, later serving as a research fellow at Leiden University (attested 2012).

Vincent Eltschinger, working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, studied at Lausanne (PhD under Tom Tillemans) and Vienna. He served at the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, including as interim director (2014–2015), and joined EPHE around 2015.

Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1992–1997). He worked at the CNRS (~1998–2012) and became Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2012.

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in Indology and history/archaeology, having studied at École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle under Bruno Dagens. He has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

Vincent Tournier, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, completed his PhD at École Pratique des Hautes Études by 2012 and studied under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub and Seishi Karashima. He held a post at École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2021).
Vincenzo Vergiani is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Raffaele Torella (~1996–2001) and held a post at the University of Cambridge around 2012.

Virendra Nath Misra was an Indian scholar of Indology and archaeology who studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953–1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961). He was Director of the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1993–2000).

Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1915–1919) and became General Editor of the Mahabharata at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in 1925.

Vishwa Nath Pathak was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was affiliated with Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, where he is attested as a professor in 1987.

Vishwanath Narayan Mandlik was an Indology scholar who studied at Elphinstone College (~1847–1851). He served as an examiner in Marathi and Law at the University of Mumbai and as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878).
Vishwanath Prasad Varma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, Kali Kinkar Datta, and Joachim Wach.
Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita.

Vladimir Minorsky was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and history/archaeology who studied at Moscow Imperial University and Lazarev Institute. He held posts at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1923–1932) and SOAS University of London (~1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Moscow State University. After lecturing at Kyung Hee University (1997–2000), he was appointed Associate Professor (2000) and then Professor (2006) at the University of Oslo.

Vladimir Vyacheslavovich Balabushevich was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested in 1970 and 1990).
